newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels ridicule offer of cabinet posts.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels ridicule offer of cabinet posts.

text.p: Zairean rebels dismissed on Friday as a joke an offer of six ministerial posts in Zaire's new government and said the U.N. refugee agency should see their leader for permission to repatriate thousands of Hutu refugees.
Gaten Kakudji, secretary-general of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL), told Reuters rebels were not interested in any such cabinet posts.
He said the AFDL's aim was to topple ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko and his government, so it could not take seriously new Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi's offer on Thursday.

"Tshisekedi's offer is little more than comedy to amuse the gallery and people of Kinshasa but it lacks all logic. He is Mobutu's prime minister and he knows our objectives but he still offers us places in Mobutu's government," Kakudji said.
"Our mission is radical change in this country...Perhaps he made the offer to distract us and to sabotage the strategy."
Kakudji said Tshisekedi or his envoys were welcome to talks at rebel headquarters in the eastern Zairean city of Goma.
He said talks in South Africa were due to open on Saturday between representatives of Mobutu and the alliance to negotiate a meeting between the president and rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
The rebels have seized a quarter of Zaire since October and are advancing on the central diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi and the second largest city Lubumbashi in the mineral-rich southeast.
Kakudji said aid agencies were authorised by the rebels to repatriate 80,000 Hutu refugees scattered south of the northeast city of Kisangani after a four-month trek through the jungle.

But he said the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR should meet Kabila to finalise permission. UNHCR wants to evacuate the weakest refugees by air through Kisangani as a transit point but the rebels refuse to allow them into the northeast capital.
"I think that there is a misunderstanding. Everything that they want has been granted except installing refugee camps. I ask UNHCR to go and see Kabila," Kakudji said in Goma.
Rebel officials said they feared UNHCR and other agencies had plans aimed at making relief work and helping Burundian and Rwandan refugees at the expense of Zaireans displaced by war.

Kakudji said aid agencies should return displaced Zaireans to their homes and give money to integrate repatriated Rwandans into Rwanda, which refugees fled in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the genocide of up to 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
The Tutsi-dominated rebels fear the refugees include Hutu former Rwandan troops and Interahamwe militiamen who had a major role in the mass slaughter in 1994 and have fought alongside Zairean troops.
The World Food Programme (WFP) said one of its staff found 4,500 refugees in very bad health hiding on Thursday in forest between 82 km and 125 km (50 and 78 miles) south of Kisangani.
"The assumption was that there were groups of 80,000 south of Kisangani but our impression is there are still more people in the jungle in an even worse state," said a WFP spokeswoman.
The leaders of the world's four biggest aid organisations launched on Thursday an unprecedented joint appeal for urgent help for refugees stranded in the war zone in eastern Zaire.

A Hutu refugee lobby group, the Rally for the Return of Refugees and Democracy to Rwanda (RDR), said on Friday monitors among the refugees had recorded the deaths of 982 refugees since March 22 because of a lack of care or at the hands of rebels.
"At this rate all the refugees will be wiped out in less than three months," said RDR, urging aid agencies to push the rebels to allow the refugees to be grouped at a single site.
It said the refugees had suffered enough and it would be a crime if the survivors died of hunger or from rebel bullets.
